"… “Unlike OpenAI, which has a bazillion dollars and can throw ten thousand agents [at a problem], this is a nice way for the community to come together,” he says. For now, though, he thinks the approach is best suited to machine learning, a field that “can be automated to quite an extent.” Other sciences—such as biology—face “the physical world bottleneck,” he says, where hypotheses must be tested with real experiments. “People are trying to automate some of that, but we’re not yet there.” …"
